faqs.a: Yes. Navy sailors must hold Australian citizenship, be at least 17 years old, and pass aptitude, medical and fitness screening. Some specialist roles, such as nuclear submarine positions, add extra security screening through the Australian Submarine Agency and partner security requirements.
faqs.q: Do I need to be an Australian citizen to join the Navy?

faqs.a: The New Entry Sailor Course lasts 10 weeks at HMAS Cerberus in Victoria. It covers drill, weapons handling, first aid, sailing and service knowledge, and includes the Navy swim test. Category training follows, with its length depending on the specialisation you choose.
faqs.q: How long is Navy recruit training?

faqs.a: In uniform, you must complete a safety jump from a 3-metre tower, swim 10 metres underwater, swim 50 metres using survival strokes, and tread water or float for 15 minutes. Swimming training before you join makes the test much easier, and Navy fitness instructors support you throughout training.
faqs.q: What does the Navy swim test involve?

faqs.a: Options include Boatswain's Mate, Combat Systems Operator, Clearance Diver, Communications and Information Systems Sailor, Chef, Dental Assistant, Hydrographic Surveyor, Medical Sailor and Musician. Each has its own training pipeline, sea and shore posting pattern, promotion path, and daily duties at sea and ashore.

headline: Become a Royal Australian Navy Sailor in 2026
metaDescription: Royal Australian Navy sailor recruitment 2026: citizenship and age rules, 10-week New Entry Sailor Course at HMAS Cerberus, swim test, roles and starting pay.

sections.content:
To join the Royal Australian Navy as a sailor you must be an Australian citizen, be at least 17 years old at enlistment, and meet aptitude, medical and fitness requirements. Applicants are assessed through questionnaires, a physical examination and the Navy's entry fitness standards before an offer is made.

There is no single sailor job. Sailors specialise in areas such as seamanship, combat systems, communications, medicine, catering, hydrography and music, so applicants should compare categories carefully and choose one that matches their strengths and interests.
sections.title: Who Can Join as a Sailor

sections.content:
All new sailors complete the 10-week New Entry Sailor Course at the Recruit School at HMAS Cerberus in Victoria. The course covers general service knowledge, drill and ceremonial procedures, weapons training, workplace safety, first aid and sailing, plus general fitness and the Navy swim test.

The swim test, completed in uniform, includes a safety jump from a 3-metre tower, a 10-metre underwater swim, a 50-metre swim using survival strokes, and treading water or floating for 15 minutes. Sailors who pass move on to category-specific employment training.
sections.title: Initial Training at HMAS Cerberus

sections.content:
Most sailors are enlisted for an initial minimum period of service of two to three years, depending on their category, with further periods offered subject to Navy requirements and suitability. Discharge can be requested at any time once any outstanding minimum service obligation is complete.

Navy life includes free medical and dental care, chef-made meals, gyms and sports facilities, and generous superannuation and housing support. Sea postings bring allowances, including maritime and submarine allowances for eligible roles, while shore postings offer more regular hours and family stability.
